note: Ps31 (54 chars). Refuge+trust in distress. chesed x3 (v7,16,21), batach x2 (v6 hate idols / v14 the turn), chasah refuge x2 (v1,19), bosh shame x4, nefesh x3 (v7,9,13), ruach commit my spirit v5, my times in your hand v15, v24 echoes Ps27:14. Poetic ledger; span-id pairs.

dims.v: 'In you, O LORD, do I TAKE REFUGE (chasah); let me never be put to shame' — the opening posture; chasah (recurs v19) the sheltering that pleads against disgrace, the ground of the whole psalm
be put to shame (bosh, negated plea)
deprecated ('let me NEVER be put to shame')
'let me never be put to SHAME (bosh)' — disgrace dreaded by the refugee; bosh opens the shame-thread (v17x2), the shame from which taking refuge should deliver
'in your RIGHTEOUSNESS (tsedaqah) deliver me' — God's righteousness as the ground of rescue; tsedaqah here the saving justice appealed to, deliverance grounded in God's own rightness
'Be a rock of refuge, a strong fortress to SAVE (yasha) me' — God as the saving stronghold; yasha (recurs v16) the rescue sought from the rock of refuge

'Into your hand I COMMIT (paqad) my spirit' — the entrusting of the whole self to God; paqad here the deliberate handing-over of one's life, the supreme act of trust (the words Christ takes up, Lk23:46)
'my SPIRIT (ruach)' — the inner life-breath entrusted to God; ruach here (contrast the literal wind of Ps18:10,42) the animating self, the whole inner person placed in God's hand
'you have REDEEMED (padah) me, O LORD, faithful God' — the ground of the committal; padah (recurs Ps25,26) the ransom already accomplished that makes entrusting the spirit reasonable
'O LORD, FAITHFUL (emeth) God' — God's faithfulness the reason to commit the spirit; emeth (recurs Ps30:9) the reliability that makes God a safe keeper of the entrusted self
'I HATE (sane) those who pay regard to worthless idols' — righteous aversion to idolatry; sane here the good hatred (as Ps26:5), set in contrast to trust in the LORD
the object of the idolaters' regard
'WORTHLESS (shav) idols' — the empty vanities the idolaters serve; shav (as Ps24:4) the false/vain thing, worthless objects of misplaced devotion
'but I TRUST (batach) in the LORD' — trust set against idolatry; batach (recurs v14) the reliance on the living God that is the alternative to worthless idols
'I will REJOICE (gil) and be glad in your steadfast love' — joy in God's chesed even mid-distress; gil the exultation grounded not in circumstance but in God's love
'and be GLAD (samach)' — gladness twinned with exultation; samach the joy in God's love, paired with gil, both resting on chesed not circumstance
'in your CHESED (steadfast love)... you have seen my affliction' — God's love that sees suffering; chesed the first of three (v7,16,21), here the love that beholds and knows the distress of the soul
'you have seen my AFFLICTION (oni)' — the misery God regards; oni (as Ps25:18) the suffering the loving God sees, the ground of comfort
know (yada - the distress of my soul)
'you have KNOWN (yada) the distress of my soul' — God's intimate knowledge of inner anguish; yada here the deep divine acquaintance with the soul's straits, matched to his seeing the affliction
'the distress of my SOUL (nefesh)' — the inner self in straits; nefesh here the anguished person God knows (first of three, v7,9,13), the soul in adversity
'Be GRACIOUS (chanan) to me, O LORD, for I am in distress' — the plea for grace amid trouble; chanan (recurs Ps30) the appeal to favour as eye, soul, and body waste with grief
'my eye is wasted from GRIEF (kaas); my soul and my body also' — sorrow consuming the whole person; kaas = grief/vexation, the anguish that wastes eye, soul, and flesh alike
'my SOUL (nefesh) and my body also' — the soul wasting with the body under grief; nefesh here the inner self worn down (second of three), suffering with the flesh
'my life is spent with SORROW (yagon), and my years with sighing' — life consumed by grief; yagon = deep sorrow, the anguish that spends his very years
'my years with SIGHING (anachah)' — the groaning that fills his days; anachah = the sigh of grief, the audible weariness of prolonged distress
'my strength fails because of my INIQUITY (avon)' — sin as a cause of the wasting; avon (recurs Ps25,18) the guilt that saps strength, distress linked to iniquity
'I have become a REPROACH (cherpah), especially to my neighbours' — social disgrace; cherpah (as Ps22:6) the scorn heaped on the sufferer, shunned even by neighbours
'an object of DREAD (pachad) to my acquaintances' — shunned as if contagious; pachad (as Ps27:1) here the terror he inspires in others, who flee from him in the street
'ACQUAINTANCES (those who know me)... flee from me' — abandonment by the familiar; yada here as the knowers/friends who now shun him, the isolation of the reproached
'I have been FORGOTTEN (shakach) like one who is dead' — erased from memory; shakach = to be forgotten, the sufferer become like a broken vessel, out of mind as the dead
'TERROR (magor) on every side! as they scheme against me' — encircling dread; magor = terror all around, the whispered plots pressing in on the life
'they PLOT (zamam) to take my life' — the deliberate scheming of the foes; zamam (as Ps17:3, there of David's good resolve; here evil) the fixed intent, now the enemies' plan against his life
life / soul (nefesh - to take my life)
'as they plot to take my LIFE (nefesh)' — the life-self the foes hunt; nefesh here (third of three, v7,9,13) the very life targeted by the schemers

'But I TRUST (batach) in you, O LORD; I say, You are my God' — the great turn from terror to trust; batach (recurs v6) the emphatic 'But I' that pivots the psalm from lament to confidence, the whole self resting on 'You are my God'
'Make your face shine on your servant; SAVE (yasha) me in your steadfast love!' — salvation grounded in God's love and shining face; yasha (recurs v2) the rescue sought as chesed acts
'save me in your CHESED (steadfast love)' — the second chesed; God's love the medium of rescue, salvation flowing from covenant loyalty
be put to shame (bosh, negated plea)
deprecated ('let me NOT be put to shame')
'let me not be put to SHAME (bosh), for I call upon you' — shame averted by calling on God; bosh (recurs v1) the disgrace the caller escapes, while the wicked's shame is invoked
'for I CALL (qara) upon you' — invocation as the guarantee against shame; qara the calling that ensures the caller will not be disgraced
'let the WICKED (resha'im) be put to shame; let them go silently to Sheol' — shame invoked on the foes; resha'im whose disgrace is the counterpart to the psalmist's vindication
be put to shame (bosh - of the wicked)
'let them be put to SHAME (bosh)' — shame reassigned to the wicked; bosh (fourth in the psalm) falls on the foes, the just reversal of the shame the psalmist feared
'Let the LYING (sheqer) lips be mute, which speak insolently against the righteous' — the false speech silenced; sheqer (as Ps27:12) the lying lips that assail the righteous in pride and contempt
'against the RIGHTEOUS (tsaddiq)' — the innocent target of the slander; tsaddiq the just one the lying lips assail with pride and contempt
'in PRIDE (gaavah) and contempt' — the arrogance behind the slander; gaavah (recurs v23) the haughtiness that speaks against the righteous, pride joined to contempt
'and CONTEMPT (buz)' — the scorn twinned with pride; buz = despising, the disdain the arrogant heap on the righteous
those who fear and take refuge
'how abundant is your GOODNESS (tov), stored up for those who fear you' — God's treasured goodness; tov (recurs Ps25,27) the kindness laid up for the God-fearers who take refuge in him
paired with those who take refuge
'stored up for those who FEAR (yare) you' — the God-fearers as recipients of goodness; yare (recurs Ps25) the reverent for whom God's goodness is treasured
those who take refuge in God
'worked for those who TAKE REFUGE (chasah) in you' — the refuge-seekers as beneficiaries; chasah (recurs v1) the sheltering that, with the fear of God, receives his stored goodness
in the cover of your presence

'In the cover of your presence you HIDE (sathar) them from the plots of men' — protective concealment; sathar here the good hiding (as Ps27:5, contrast Ps30:7) — God shelters his own in his presence from the strife of tongues
'BLESSED (barak) be the LORD, for he has wondrously shown his steadfast love' — praise for chesed displayed; barak (as Ps28:6) the blessing of God for his marvellous love in the besieged city

'he has wondrously shown his CHESED (steadfast love) to me' — the third chesed; God's love marvellously displayed in the siege, the ground of the blessing (chesed frames the psalm: v7 seen, v16 saving, v21 shown)
'LOVE (aheb) the LORD, all you his saints!' — the call to love God; aheb (as Ps26:8) the affection commanded of the whole covenant community, the fitting response to his preserving love
'all you his SAINTS (chasidim)' — the covenant-loyal summoned to love; chasid (recurs Ps30:4) the chesed-bearers called to love the God who shows them chesed
faithful (emun - the LORD preserves the faithful)
'The LORD preserves the FAITHFUL (emun) but abundantly repays the proud' — the faithful kept, the proud repaid; emun = faithfulness/steadiness, the loyal ones God guards, set against the arrogant
the one who acts in pride
'abundantly repays the one who acts in PRIDE (gaavah)' — the proud requited; gaavah (recurs v18) the arrogance God repays, the opposite of the faithful he preserves
all who wait for the LORD
paired with the heart taking courage

'Be STRONG (chazaq), and let your heart take courage, all you who wait for the LORD!' — the closing exhortation; chazaq (echoes Ps27:14 verbatim) the strength commanded of all who wait, sealing the psalm as Ps27 did
heart (lev - let your heart take courage)
'let your HEART (lev) take courage' — the heart summoned to strength; lev (echoes Ps27:14) the seat exhorted to courage in the waiting, the inner correlate of being strong
of the heart, paired with being strong
'let your heart TAKE COURAGE (amets)' — courage as the waiting heart's resolve; amets (echoes Ps27:14) the emboldening paired with chazaq, the closing counsel to all who wait on the LORD

v3: 'for your NAME'S sake you lead me and guide me' - God's guidance grounded in his own name/honour; the leading and guiding of the trusting soul, deliverance motivated by God's reputation, not the psalmist's merit

v22: 'I had said in my ALARM, I am cut off from your sight. But you HEARD the voice of my pleas' - panic confessed and answered; the hasty despair ('cut off') corrected by God's hearing, the alarm of the moment overturned by the God who listens
my times in your hand -> rescue (natsal)

v15: 'My TIMES are in your hand; RESCUE me from the hand of my enemies' - the whole span of life surrendered to God's control; the deepest resolve of the trust (v14) - every moment held in God's hand, the ground on which rescue from the enemy's hand is sought (God's hand vs the foe's hand)
